title: Quick sort
objective: Partition around a pivot, then sort each side, and see how a bad pivot slows it down.

sources.title: Cormen, Leiserson, Rivest and Stein, Introduction to Algorithms, 4th ed. (MIT Press, 2022): quicksort and the partition procedure

simplifies: The pivot here is always the last item, so already-sorted input is the worst case. Real versions pick a random or median-of-three pivot to avoid that.

quiz.prompt: After partitioning around pivot 5, which is guaranteed?

options.text: Everything left of 5 is smaller and 5 is in its final place
options.explanation: Right. That is why each side can then be sorted on its own.
Only the pivot is placed; each side still needs sorting.

options.text: Both sides have the same size
options.explanation: Sizes depend on the pivot; a bad pivot gives very uneven sides.

quiz.prompt: With "last item as pivot", which input is slowest?

options.explanation: Right. Each pivot is the largest, so one side is empty and the other loses just one item: O(n²).
Random order tends to give balanced splits: about n log n.
Distinct values are fine; the order is what makes it slow.
